chunk_findings.detail: The new `EC.commit_at` can advance `wt.base` after `landed_before` has already been captured on the preceding line. When the primary has an uncommitted shard, `EC.commit_at` creates a new commit on the base branch before `W.merge` runs. If the merge then fails (for example, the existing conflict path where `c.txt` conflicts), `_landed_anyway` is called with the stale pre-event SHA while the base has already moved to the event commit. The branch has not landed—the modified test still asserts `main:c.txt` is unchanged—but the landing-check helper receives a baseline that no longer represents the state before the merge attempt, so it can misclassify the failure or report a false “landed anyway” note. The event commit should happen before `landed_before` is read, or `landed_before` should be refreshed after `EC.commit_at`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:188

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at` runs before `W.merge` and does not know whether the merge will succeed. In the refusal case with a primary event shard plus a `c.txt` conflict, `main` gets a new shard commit and only then `W.merge` returns `REFUSED`; the CLI reports failure but the primary branch has moved. The change acknowledges this by deleting the old `rev-parse HEAD` equality assertion in `tests/test_merge_primary_clean.py` and replacing it with a weaker `main:c.txt` content check, so a failed merge no longer guarantees the primary was left where it was.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:188

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at(log, cfg, "merge", f"merge {item}")` is called unconditionally during `merge` even when the merge will ultimately fail due to file conflicts (such as in `test_merge_primary_clean` where `c.txt` conflicts). This causes the primary's uncommitted event shards to be committed to `main` as part of a failed merge operation, altering the repository state and committing uncommitted work even though the merge itself was refused and rolled back.

chunk_findings.detail: The new project-override discovery hardcodes the external filesystem layout `.ddflow/harnesses.d` and reads descriptor files directly via `Path.is_dir`, `Path.glob`, and `Path.read_text` inside the service. Project guidance [r-adapters] requires filesystem layout and external file access to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, so tests can fake the filesystem and layout changes touch one place. Given any project root with `.ddflow/harnesses.d/foo.toml`, `load_in` bypasses the adapter layer and accesses the project directory directly, violating that rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:project_dir

chunk_findings.detail: The test named “replaces the shipped descriptor” never exercises the user-visible path (`harness_show`) for an overridden existing agent, and the dict comprehension hides duplicate descriptors. For example, if `harness_show(tmp_path, "claude")` still resolves `claude` from `harnessreg.load()` first, or if `load_in` returns `[shipped_claude, project_claude]` instead of removing the shipped descriptor, the assertion `by_id["claude"].family == "demo"` still passes because the project descriptor is last in the dict, while `harness show claude` would still show the shipped descriptor. The regression test should call `harness_show(tmp_path, "claude")` and assert the overridden values (and/or assert exactly one descriptor with that id).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_project_override.py:34

chunk_findings.detail: The new project override path is read directly from the filesystem layout (`Path(root) / ".ddflow" / "harnesses.d"`, then `_parse_dir` calls `glob`/`read_text`) instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. Rule r-adapters explicitly includes filesystem layout as an external dependency. A test or alternate project-layout implementation that substitutes the filesystem adapter cannot intercept this hard-coded `.ddflow/harnesses.d` logic, so `load_in` silently misses or reads imprecisely the override directory in that environment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/harnessreg.py:load_in / project_dir [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: This test claims to prove a new agent in `.ddflow/harnesses.d` changes `harness show`, but it writes `_GOOD`, whose descriptor id is `demo`, to `demo.toml`. The shipped harness directory already contains `demo` (this is the descriptor `_GOOD` mirrors), so `harness_show(tmp_path, "demo")` returns the shipped demo even if `load_in` completely ignores the project directory: `out.exit == 0` and `out.data["id"] == "demo"` both pass. The regression test therefore does not actually exercise project-only agents and would not catch the original “project directory is not read” bug. Use a project-only id that is not in the shipped harness set.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_project_override.py:test_a_new_agent_in_the_project_dir_changes_harness_show

chunk_findings.detail: The new `EC.commit_at` runs unconditionally before `W.merge` and is not rolled back when the merge is refused. Given the existing conflict-test setup (base and branch both modify `c.txt`) plus the new test’s dirty primary shard `.ddflow/events/shared.jsonl`, line 188 commits that dirty shard onto `main`; `W.merge` then still fails on the `c.txt` conflict, so the merge command returns `REFUSED` while `main` has advanced to a new commit containing uncommitted shard data (possibly from other work). The removed assertion in `tests/test_merge_primary_clean.py` that HEAD was unchanged after a refused merge was the guard for this; replacing it with a `main:c.txt` check hides the side effect.

chunk_findings.detail: The change introduces a new filesystem-layout dependency directly in the service layer: `project_dir()` hard-codes `.ddflow/harnesses.d`, and `load_in()` then uses `Path.is_dir()`, `Path.glob()`, and `Path.read_text()` to discover and parse project descriptor files. Under [r-adapters], filesystem layout and TOML/file reading are external dependencies that must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; this new project-override path bypasses that boundary, so a filesystem-layout change or a fake-filesystem test cannot be handled by swapping an adapter implementation.

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for overriding a shipped descriptor never exercises `harness_show`; it only checks `harnessreg.load_in`. Given a project override for `claude` as written, the assertion can still pass while `harness show claude` continues to resolve the shipped descriptor through a shipped-only path (for example, if `harness_show` special-cases existing shipped ids or still calls `harnessreg.load()` for them). In that scenario the user-visible behavior described in the bug/fix intent—project overrides changing `harness show`—is broken, but this “regression test” does not fail, so it does not actually guard the stated regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_project_override.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_parse_dir`/`project_dir`/`load_in` code reads `.ddflow/harnesses.d` directly via `Path.glob`, `Path.read_text`, and `Path.is_dir` from `ddflow/services/harnessreg.py`. This is a new filesystem-layout dependency handled outside `ddflow/adapters`, which violates [r-adapters] (filesystem layout must go through a port, with tests using a fake instead of the real filesystem). The change should introduce an adapter port for the project override directory rather than adding direct disk access in the service.

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not actually verify that a shipped descriptor is overridden. It starts from `_GOOD` with `id = "demo"`, changes the id to `"claude"`, writes `claude.toml`, and only asserts `by_id["claude"].family == "demo"`. Because the project file itself contains `family = "demo"`, that assertion holds if `load_in` merely appends project descriptors to the shipped list without replacing any existing descriptor; both `demo` and `claude` would be present and the test would pass. A regression test for B-drv-descriptor-override-missing should use a project file for an existing shipped descriptor id (or assert the shipped descriptor’s value changed/old id is replaced), otherwise the bug can remain undetected.
